question: Water flows at a constant rate of $5\ \text{m}^3/\text{min}$ into a horizontal trough of length $10\ \text{m}$. Each end of the trough is an isosceles triangle of height $2\ \text{m}$ and top width $4\ \text{m}$. When the water has depth $h$ metres, its surface width is $w$ metres. Because the water cross-section is similar to the triangular end of the trough, the width and depth remain proportional as the water level rises.(a) Establish the relation between $w$ and $h$.(b) Express the volume of water in terms of $h$.(c) Determine the rate at which the depth is increasing when $h=1\ \text{m}$.(d) Find the rate of increase of the surface width at this instant and the time required for the depth to rise from $1\ \text{m}$ to $1.5\ \text{m}$.
explanation: (a)By similarity of the water cross-section and the triangular end,`\frac{w}{h}=\frac{4}{2}=2`Therefore,`w=2h`(b)The cross-sectional area of the water is`A=\frac{1}{2}wh`Using $w=2h$,`A=\frac{1}{2}(2h)h=h^2`Since the trough is $10\ \text{m}$ long, its water volume is`V=10h^2`(c)Differentiating $V=10h^2$ with respect to time,`\frac{dV}{dt}=20h\frac{dh}{dt}`At $h=1\ \text{m}$ and $\frac{dV}{dt}=5\ \text{m}^3/\text{min}$,`5=20(1)\frac{dh}{dt}\frac{dh}{dt}=\frac{1}{4}\ \text{m/min}`(d)Since $w=2h$,`\frac{dw}{dt}=2\frac{dh}{dt}=2\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)=\frac{1}{2}\ \text{m/min}`At $h=1$, the volume is`V_1=10(1)^2=10\ \text{m}^3`At $h=1.5$,`V_2=10(1.5)^2=22.5\ \text{m}^3`The required increase in volume is $12.5\ \text{m}^3$. Hence, the required time is`t=\frac{12.5}{5}=2.5\ \text{minutes}`
